digo: Mvamva wa tsakani; Mphvamva tsaka (App. VI)

teaser.en: The forest double of a grassland shrub, though botanists put the two in different families.

summary.en: Mvamva wa tsakani is Memecylon sansibaricum, a shrub or small tree of coastal forest. The Digo see it as the forest form of Mvamva, a Millettia of the bushed grassland.

about.en: Mvamva wa tsakani is an evergreen shrub or small tree with opposite, leathery, glossy leaves whose side veins are almost invisible. Like other Memecylons it bears clusters of small blue to purple flowers on the older twigs, followed by small round berries that ripen dark purple or black.

where.en: It grows in the coastal forests and thickets of Kenya and Tanzania.

culture.en: The name shows how Digo naming pairs plants by habitat: a forest plant is named after a look-alike from the open country and marked tsaka or wa tsakani, 'of the forest'.

names.en: Pakia's Appendix III gives Mvamva wa tsakani; Appendix VI writes it Mphvamva tsaka and explains it as 'forest Millettia', the forest type of Mphamva (Millettia usaramensis), which grows in bushed grassland. No shared names are recorded. Its scientific name is Memecylon sansibaricum.

reason.en: The grassland Mvamva it is named after
